stem:
Sia compares changes in the lab: a magnesium ribbon burns in air with heat and light; a sealed oxygen-free mixture still releases heat; and a classmate asks whether nitrogen is the gas that lets magnesium burn.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The magnesium ribbon burning in air is combustion because it reacts with oxygen and produces heat and light.
A reaction with oxygen that releases heat can still be combustion even when no large flame is seen.
Nitrogen is the gas required for the magnesium ribbon to burn.
The oxygen-free mixture that releases heat is also combustion.

teacher.key_rationale: Combustion needs reaction with oxygen plus heat or light. Nitrogen is the wrong gas, and an oxygen-free heat release fails the oxygen condition. A flameless oxygen reaction that still releases heat can still count as combustion.
